scenes.dialogue: Hi, I am Advocate Ravi from LawWorld. Can a company delay collecting an arbitral award to extend challenge limits?
scenes.visual3D: Advocate Ravi smiling and speaking directly to camera against a solid plain grey studio background

scenes.dialogue: A petrol dealer operated since 1959. After a 2017 inspection terminated the dealership, dispute went to arbitration.
scenes.visual3D: Advocate Ravi presenting topic professionally against a solid plain grey studio background

scenes.dialogue: On 15 February 2024, the award passed. Next day, the Centre notified both sides: pay dues, collect copies.
scenes.visual3D: Advocate Ravi speaking earnestly against a solid plain grey studio background

scenes.dialogue: The dealer collected by 5 March. The company paid on 28 March and collected on 22 April.
scenes.visual3D: Advocate Ravi analyzing case timeline against a solid plain grey studio background

scenes.dialogue: The company filed its Section 34 petition on 18 July, counting three months from 22 April collection.
scenes.visual3D: Advocate Ravi explaining legal filing dates against a solid plain grey studio background

scenes.dialogue: The High Court held: paying dues was entirely in company control, so limitation ran from availability.
scenes.visual3D: Advocate Ravi detailing High Court decision against a solid plain grey studio background

scenes.dialogue: No one can take advantage of their own wrong. The Section 34 petition was barred by limitation.
scenes.visual3D: Advocate Ravi emphasizing legal principles against a solid plain grey studio background

scenes.dialogue: Lesson: once the award is ready, the clock ticks. Follow LawWorld for judgments that change how you file!
scenes.visual3D: Advocate Ravi concluding presentation warmly against a solid plain grey studio background
